verdict.rationale: GitHub's docs describe fine-grained personal access tokens that carry an explicit set of permissions limiting which resources the token can reach via the API [github-docs-19, github-docs-21, github-docs-42]. The X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions response header tells you which permissions an endpoint needs, which supports issuing least-privilege tokens [github-docs-18]. Nothing in the pack ties these tokens to agents specifically, but they serve the story's core as written. Missing for 10: evidence of repository-level scoping, expiration or revocation controls, and agent-specific credentials (e.g., app-based identities); no independent or hands-on corroboration.
